note: A shared vocabulary of shot types so a generated script says 'insert-detail on the failure point' instead of 'insert b-roll here'. Authored conventions drawn from standard film grammar, not measured results.

shots.name: Talking head
shots.purpose: Carry an argument in the speaker's own voice.
shots.useWhen: The credibility of the claim rests on who is making it.
shots.avoidWhen: The claim is visual and would be better shown than asserted.

shots.name: Establishing
shots.purpose: Place the viewer in a location or context.
shots.useWhen: The setting itself is part of the proof.
shots.avoidWhen: Opening a short-form video — it costs the first two seconds and earns nothing.

shots.name: Insert detail
shots.purpose: Isolate the one object or region the narration is about.
shots.useWhen: You just named a specific thing and the viewer cannot find it in a wide shot.
shots.avoidWhen: Nothing specific has been named yet.

shots.name: Hands-on product
shots.purpose: Show scale, texture, and that a real object exists.
shots.useWhen: The product is physical and the audience is product-aware.

shots.name: Screen capture
shots.purpose: Demonstrate a software claim in the product itself.
shots.useWhen: The claim is 'it does X' and X is visible on screen.
shots.avoidWhen: The UI is too dense to read at the target resolution.

shots.name: Cutaway
shots.purpose: Cover an edit or compress time without a visible jump.
shots.useWhen: You removed a pause, a stumble, or a long wait.
shots.avoidWhen: It has no relationship to the narration — an unmotivated cutaway reads as filler.

shots.name: Before / after
shots.purpose: Show a change by holding everything else constant.
shots.useWhen: The transformation is the entire claim.
shots.avoidWhen: The two states differ in more than one variable; the viewer will notice and discount both.

shots.name: Over the shoulder
shots.purpose: Put the viewer behind the operator's eyes.
shots.useWhen: The viewer is meant to imagine doing the thing themselves.
shots.avoidWhen: The screen or workpiece is unreadable from that angle.

shots.name: Direct address
shots.purpose: Break the fourth wall to issue a command or a question.
shots.useWhen: Opening a pattern-interrupt hook, or closing on a call to action.
shots.avoidWhen: The middle of an explanation, where it reads as a sales turn.

shots.name: Data on screen
shots.purpose: Render a number the narration cannot carry alone.
shots.useWhen: The figure is precise and load-bearing.
shots.avoidWhen: The number is approximate — on-screen text implies a precision you may not have.

shots.name: Reaction
shots.purpose: Show a person receiving the result rather than describing it.
shots.useWhen: The emotional payoff matters more than the mechanism.
shots.avoidWhen: The reaction is staged and the audience is ad-literate.

shots.name: Static hold
shots.purpose: Stop all motion to force attention onto a single line of narration.
shots.useWhen: The most important sentence in the script.
shots.avoidWhen: More than once per short-form video.
